title: Transmission, load shape, permitting, and supply-chain source verification

verification_protocol.identity_check: Confirm the page or artifact is hosted by the named government agency, regulator, system operator, national laboratory, or official project program.
verification_protocol.claim_check: Read the page, table, or report section that supports the retained statement; do not rely on a search-result snippet.
verification_protocol.independence_rule: A second source is used when it materially tests status, capacity semantics, or a consequential interpretation. Two pages repeating the same developer statement are not treated as independent confirmation.
verification_protocol.vintage_rule: Every current-status assertion carries a date. Older technical reports remain valid only for explicitly historical evidence.
verification_protocol.capacity_rule: Nominal voltage, conductor capability, converter rating, transfer capability, transmission-service rights, contracted delivery, and capacity accreditation are separate fields. None is silently substituted for another.
verification_protocol.scenario_rule: Modeled transmission expansion is labeled scenario output, not a forecast or construction commitment.

sources.title: Hourly Electric Grid Monitor and Form EIA-930 data
sources.identity_verification: The EIA page identifies the Hourly Electric Grid Monitor as EIA's balancing-authority and regional electricity product.
sources.claim_verification: The downloaded 2024 balance and subregion files contain hour-ending local and UTC timestamps, demand, adjusted demand, forecast, generation, interchange, BA, region, and subregion fields. Local hashes and row validation are recorded in load-shape/coverage.json.
sources.limitations: BA reporting and adjustment practices vary; EIA-930 demand is not sector-attributed consumption.

sources.title: Electric Power Transmission Lines
sources.publisher: Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data / U.S. Department of Homeland Security
sources.identity_verification: The Data.gov catalog names HIFLD as publisher and links the ArcGIS feature service.
sources.claim_verification: The service schema contains route geometry, owner, status, source date, validation method, voltage, and voltage class. It does not contain an MW rating field. The local >=230 kV query returned 10,031 features.
sources.limitations: Catalog metadata says the dataset was last updated in 2022; feature source dates vary and this is not a real-time power-flow model.

sources.title: Does EIA have maps or data on the location of electric power plants and transmission lines in the United States?
sources.claim_verification: EIA points users to the HIFLD transmission-line layer and states that EIA and HIFLD do not publish substation locations.
sources.limitations: Explains public availability; it is not an electrical network dataset.

sources.title: Governor Mills Welcomes Completion of New England Clean Energy Connect Project
sources.publisher: Office of Governor Janet T. Mills, State of Maine
sources.claim_verification: The announcement says construction was completed, power was flowing, and the project can deliver 1,200 MW from Quebec to New England.
sources.limitations: Government completion announcement; operational market qualification is separately checked against ISO-NE.

sources.title: 2020 Annual Report
sources.claim_verification: The report describes a 145-mile, 1,200 MW HVDC line from the Quebec-Maine border to Lewiston and the May 3, 2019 CPCN.
sources.limitations: Historical siting record, not current operations.

sources.title: DOE/EA-2155 New England Clean Energy Connect
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE NEPA project record and PDF.
sources.claim_verification: The assessment describes the international project, a plus/minus 320 kV DC configuration, and a 1,200 MW converter to 345 kV AC.
sources.limitations: Design and environmental-review record; later completion is verified separately.

sources.title: 2026 Transmission Transfer Capabilities Update
sources.claim_verification: The planning table shows 1,200 MW NECEC energy-import capability with zero capacity-import capability in the modeled period, and 2,000 MW Phase II energy-import capability with 1,400 MW capacity-import capability. It notes NECEC commercial operation on December 31, 2025.
sources.limitations: Study-case transfer assumptions and capacity-import treatment are not universal real-time operating limits.

sources.title: Tier 4 Renewable Energy Program
sources.publisher: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority
sources.claim_verification: The page identifies CHPE as a 339-mile, 1,250 MW HVDC project and lists commercial operation on May 13, 2026.
sources.limitations: Project specification and status; not a time-varying transfer-limit series.

sources.title: Governor Hochul Celebrates Completion of Champlain Hudson Power Express Project
sources.publisher: Office of the Governor, State of New York
sources.claim_verification: Independently confirms project completion and the 339-mile Canada-to-New York City route; gives an expected annual delivery figure of 10.4 TWh.
sources.limitations: Expected energy delivery is not the same as capacity or an hourly guarantee.

sources.title: Pacific Direct Current Intertie
sources.claim_verification: BPA describes the plus/minus 500 kV intertie, current 3,100 MW transfer capability, and an upgrade target of 3,220 MW for its portion.
sources.limitations: The upgrade target is separate from current capability and does not replace operating constraints.

sources.title: Order No. 881 HVDC Transmission Operating Agreement attachment
sources.claim_verification: The document describes Phase I nominal capability of 690 MW and Phase II nominal transfer capability of 2,000 MW, while noting actual operation can be below the nominal value.
sources.limitations: Nominal transfer capability must not be presented as a constant dispatch level.

sources.title: Amount of Capacity Suppliers Are Qualified to Offer
sources.claim_verification: The document lists unforced-capacity delivery-right quantities for Cross Sound Cable (330 MW), Neptune (660 MW), Linden VFT (315 MW), and Hudson Transmission Project (660 MW).
sources.limitations: These are transmission-service/capacity-delivery rights, not conductor thermal ratings.

sources.title: 2011-2012 Transmission Plan
sources.claim_verification: The plan identifies the operating Trans Bay Cable as a unidirectional 400 MW HVDC facility into San Francisco.
sources.limitations: Historical plan; retained for stable project design characteristics.

sources.title: Presidential Permit PP-305, Montana Alberta Tie Ltd.
sources.claim_verification: The permit describes the 230 kV international line and maximum nonsimultaneous transfer limits of 300 MW northbound and 325 MW southbound.
sources.limitations: Permitted maxima are not a real-time schedule.

sources.title: Building Electric Transmission Lines: A Review of Recent Transmission Projects
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy / Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
sources.claim_verification: The Great Northern case describes roughly 224 miles of 500 kV AC transmission designed for 883 MW and documents routing, review, and stakeholder practices across recent projects.
sources.limitations: Case studies are historical and do not establish current status for every project.

sources.title: One Nevada Line
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy Loan Programs Office
sources.claim_verification: DOE identifies a 235-mile, 500 kV, 600 MW line with commercial operation beginning in January 2014.
sources.limitations: Project design capacity, not a dynamic operating limit.

sources.title: Minnesota Power Transmission: Great Northern Transmission Line
sources.claim_verification: The current transmission page says construction began in January 2017 and the line was energized and began delivering hydropower in June 2020.
sources.limitations: Confirms operating status; the design-capacity quantity comes from the DOE/LBNL case study.

sources.title: Transmission Development Forum: Ten West Link update
sources.claim_verification: The update reports approximately 125 miles, 3,200 MW conductor capability, and a 2,400 MW series-compensation-station equipment limit. CAISO later reported the line energized in June 2024.
sources.limitations: The two capacities describe different components; neither is presented as a universal interface limit.

sources.title: SunZia Southwest Transmission Project
sources.claim_verification: The project record describes two 500 kV lines over roughly 520 miles and an ultimate permitted proposal capable of up to 4,500 MW. Current phase capacity is separately represented as 3,000 MW based on system-operator material.
sources.limitations: Ultimate permitted configuration is not current in-service capacity.

sources.title: TransWest Express Transmission Project NEPA
sources.claim_verification: WAPA describes an approximately 728-mile HVDC project with about 3,000 MW capacity.
sources.limitations: Project design capacity; construction and commercial milestones must be dated.

sources.title: Grain Belt Express Final Environmental Impact Statement
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE NEPA record and PDF.
sources.claim_verification: The FEIS describes a full bipolar plus/minus 600 kV design of about 5,000 MW, with Phase 1 about 2,500 MW and a possible later Phase 2 adding about 2,500 MW toward PJM.
sources.limitations: Design stages are proposals and injection rights constrain delivered capability.

sources.title: North Plains Connector Draft Environmental Impact Statement
sources.claim_verification: The draft describes a proposed 525 kV HVDC, approximately 420-mile, 3,000 MW bidirectional connection between Montana and North Dakota.
sources.limitations: Draft EIS; not a final approval or construction commitment.

sources.title: Transmission Facilitation Program Project Selections
sources.claim_verification: DOE lists Southern Spirit at 3,000 MW bidirectional over about 320 miles, Aroostook at 1,200 MW over about 111 miles, and Cimarron Link with 1,900 MW of firm point-to-point service over about 400 miles.
sources.limitations: Program selection and capacity contract are development milestones, not proof of operation.

sources.title: National Transmission Planning Study Executive Summary
sources.claim_verification: Across the identified central decarbonization accelerated-planning cases, total U.S. transmission grows to 2.4-3.5 times the 2020 grid by 2050. The study reports modeled savings of $270-$490 billion for accelerated expansion and $170-$380 billion from regional coordination through 2050.
sources.limitations: Results are scenario- and model-dependent, not forecasts; ranges must retain their scenario context.

sources.title: National Transmission Needs Study
sources.claim_verification: The study reports median within-region expansion by 2035 of 20% in moderate-load/moderate-clean cases, 64% in high-clean cases, and 128% in high-load cases, relative to the modeled baseline.
sources.limitations: Scenario result; not a project list or forecast.

sources.title: 2026 National Transmission Needs Study
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE page identifies the 2026 document as a draft for comment.
sources.claim_verification: DOE's draft summary emphasizes renewed load growth and reports that congestion is often concentrated in a small share of hours; it identifies areas with high within-region congestion potential.
sources.limitations: Draft, subject to revision. Dashboard must label it DRAFT and not merge it silently with the final 2023 study.

sources.title: 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment
sources.identity_verification: Official NERC assessment page and report.
sources.claim_verification: NERC reports projected 2025-2035 peak growth of roughly 224 GW in summer and 246 GW in winter, identifies data centers as a major driver, and warns that approvals and supply chains affect the pace of infrastructure additions.
sources.limitations: North American assessment-area scope; planning projections are not observed demand.

sources.title: Interregional Transfer Capability Study Final Report
sources.claim_verification: The study evaluates transfer capability and prudent interface additions for reliability under specified stress cases.
sources.limitations: Reliability-only analysis; interface additions are case-specific and do not constitute an economic project plan or a single nationally additive target.

sources.title: Transmission Planning and Cost Allocation Final Rule Explainer
sources.claim_verification: Order No. 1920 requires long-term regional planning with a horizon of at least 20 years, evaluation of benefits, cost-allocation processes, and state engagement.
sources.limitations: Planning and cost allocation do not themselves authorize, finance, or construct a line.

sources.title: Order No. 1920 Compliance Filings Schedule
sources.claim_verification: The table gives region-specific initial and interregional compliance deadlines that extend through 2027.
sources.limitations: A filing deadline is not an implementation or construction-completion date.

sources.title: Siting of Interstate Electric Transmission Facilities Explainer
sources.claim_verification: Order No. 1977 implements FERC's limited Federal Power Act section 216 backstop-siting authority and landowner-engagement requirements.
sources.limitations: This is not general federal siting authority for every interstate line.

sources.title: Coordinated Interagency Transmission Authorizations and Permits Program
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE program page and standard schedule.
sources.claim_verification: CITAP coordinates federal reviews through DOE and targets a standard two-year federal environmental-review and authorization schedule after defined preapplication and notice milestones.
sources.limitations: The two-year federal schedule is not total project-development time; state, local, Tribal, land, procurement, financing, and construction work remain.

sources.title: National Interest Electric Transmission Corridor Designation Process
sources.claim_verification: The page describes the phased NIETC process and makes clear that a designation identifies a geographic area, not a particular route or approved project.
sources.limitations: Potential corridors and designations are not construction approvals.

sources.title: FERC Rule to Improve Transmission Line Ratings
sources.claim_verification: Order No. 881 requires ambient-adjusted ratings and greater transparency to replace less accurate static assumptions where applicable.
sources.limitations: Implementation timing varies by region; a rating change does not eliminate stability, voltage, or contingency constraints.

sources.title: Grid-Enhancing Technologies Improve Existing Power Lines
sources.claim_verification: DOE describes dynamic line ratings, power-flow controls, topology optimization, and sensors as tools that can increase use of existing assets in suitable locations.
sources.limitations: Reported percentage gains are examples or study results, not universal multipliers.

sources.title: Electric Grid Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: The report maps large-power-transformer and HVDC inputs, including grain-oriented electrical steel, copper/continuous-transposed conductor, cores, windings, tanks, bushings, tap changers, insulation, cooling systems, converter valves, cable, manufacturing, testing, and heavy transport. It documents limited domestic capacity and custom-engineering constraints as of its publication.
sources.limitations: Lead-time and market-share figures are 2022-vintage unless refreshed by a current source.

sources.title: Large Power Transformer Resilience Report
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE report signed by the Secretary of Energy.
sources.claim_verification: The report addresses long procurement cycles, limited interchangeability, transportation difficulty, emergency spares, standardization, and domestic manufacturing resilience for large power transformers.
sources.limitations: Recommendations and illustrative configurations are not a live manufacturer order book.

sources.title: Electricity Grid Resilience: Climate Change Is Expected to Have Far-reaching Effects and DOE and FERC Should Take Actions
sources.claim_verification: GAO identifies long and increasing transformer lead times, limited manufacturing capacity, labor and material shortages, high unit and transport cost, and tradeoffs in standardization and stockpiling. GAO's recommendation-status text remained open in 2026.
sources.limitations: Cost and lead-time examples are not a complete census of current orders.

sources.title: DOE Finalizes Energy Efficiency Standards for Distribution Transformers
sources.claim_verification: DOE describes compliance flexibility in the final efficiency standard and cites a national-laboratory projection that distribution-transformer installations may roughly triple by 2050.
sources.limitations: Installation projection is not an order-book forecast; distribution and large power transformers are separate categories.

sources.title: Solar Photovoltaics Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Maps polysilicon, ingot, wafer, cell, module, inverter, racking, installation, and end-of-life stages and discusses geographic concentration and traceability risks.
sources.limitations: 2022 market shares require refresh before a current-value graphic.

sources.title: Wind Energy Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Maps blades, towers, nacelles, generators, gearboxes, castings/forgings, magnets, logistics, ports, vessels, workforce, and recycling; distinguishes mature land-based and emerging offshore chains.
sources.limitations: 2022 market state; project cancellations and newer policy changes require current overlays.

sources.title: Nuclear Energy Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Maps uranium conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication, nuclear-grade forgings and components, quality assurance, construction, operations, workforce, and spent-fuel stages.
sources.limitations: Advanced-reactor and HALEU availability needs a newer program-status overlay.

sources.title: Energy Storage Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Maps lithium-ion raw materials, processing, active materials, cells, packs, integration, and recycling, and compares non-lithium storage pathways such as pumped storage, flow batteries, hydrogen, and compressed air.
sources.limitations: 2022 market shares require refresh; storage power and energy capacity must remain separate.

sources.title: 2021-2024 Four Year Review of Supply Chains for the Advanced Batteries Sector
sources.claim_verification: Updates the chain from extraction and refining through precursor and active materials, cells, packs, EV/grid applications, reuse, and recycling.
sources.limitations: Announcements and funded capacity are not necessarily commissioned output.

sources.title: Hydropower Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Describes mature fleet-support capabilities while identifying scaling needs for upgrades and new construction and domestic constraints for large steel castings, forgings, and generator windings.
sources.limitations: Project-specific civil works and relicensing dominate many schedules and are not reducible to a component list.

sources.title: Water Electrolyzers and Fuel Cells Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Maps catalysts and critical materials including platinum-group metals, membranes, stacks, balance-of-plant equipment, manufacturing, hydrogen storage, and infrastructure needs for a nascent sector.
sources.limitations: The report notes limited market data; electrolyzer electricity use must not be added to demand without scenario accounting.

sources.title: Semiconductor Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Covers power semiconductors, including wide-bandgap devices used in EVs, chargers, solar/wind inverters, motor drives, and high-voltage conversion equipment.
sources.limitations: Detailed capacity and price data are rapidly changing and require current manufacturer or government statistics.

sources.title: Supply Chain Assessment for the Electric Grid's Digital Components
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE CESER page and linked report.
sources.claim_verification: Describes opaque and dynamic global supply chains for ubiquitous digital and operational-technology components and the risk of untrusted suppliers and compromised components.
sources.limitations: Security-sensitive asset-level data are intentionally not public.

sources.title: Bottleneck to Breakthrough: Rebuilding the U.S. Gas Turbine Supply Chain
sources.claim_verification: DOE describes gas-turbine manufacturing constraints in specialized hot-section components, castings and forgings, skilled labor, testing, factory investment cycles, and competition with aerospace and semiconductor supply chains.
sources.limitations: Some market lead-time examples in the report are attributed to industry or trade sources and must remain source-attributed rather than presented as a DOE census.

sources.title: Planned U.S. natural gas combined-cycle additions face equipment and regulatory uncertainty
sources.identity_verification: Official EIA Today in Energy page.
sources.claim_verification: EIA reports that planned combined-cycle additions face turbine-equipment availability and regulatory uncertainty and distinguishes reported planned capacity from completed projects.
sources.limitations: Generator survey plans can change; planned capacity is not a manufacturing order book.

sources.title: Carbon Capture, Transport, and Storage Supply Chain Deep Dive Assessment
sources.identity_verification: Official DOE page and linked report.
sources.claim_verification: The assessment maps capture equipment and chemicals, compression, CO2 pipelines and transport, storage-site characterization, injection wells, monitoring, and closure. It assesses general material risks as lower than several other clean-energy chains while emphasizing scale-up and infrastructure integration.
sources.limitations: Low general-material risk does not imply easy permitting, siting, finance, pore-space access, or pipeline buildout.

sources.title: Avoidance and Minimization Measures: Power Lines
sources.claim_verification: Describes bird collision and electrocution hazards and mitigation through siting, design, marking, and—where appropriate—burial.
sources.limitations: Risk and mitigation effectiveness are species-, voltage-, and site-specific.

sources.title: Interim Guidance for NEPA Reviews of Electric Transmission Projects
sources.claim_verification: The guidance organizes transmission review under NEPA and related statutes, including NHPA section 106, Clean Water Act section 404, Endangered Species Act, Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act, and Migratory Bird Treaty Act.
sources.limitations: Procedural guidance; project-specific effects and required permits depend on route and federal nexus.

sources.title: Electromagnetic Fields and Cancer
sources.claim_verification: NCI explains that power-frequency fields are non-ionizing and not known to damage DNA directly. It reports no consistent evidence linking non-ionizing EMF sources with cancer overall, while accurately retaining the limited childhood-leukemia evidence behind IARC's 'possibly carcinogenic' classification for ELF magnetic fields.
sources.limitations: Risk communication must preserve both the overall evidence conclusion and the limited high-exposure epidemiologic signal.

sources.title: Electrical Safety in the Workplace
sources.publisher: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health / CDC
sources.claim_verification: NIOSH identifies electrocution, shock, burns/arc blast, and falls as electrical injuries and notes that utility and construction industries had the highest rates of electricity-related injuries with days away from work in its cited 2018-2020 data.
sources.limitations: Safety overview; not a transmission-project incident-rate series.

sources.title: Transmission Impact Assessment
sources.claim_verification: Under the study's enhanced regional and interregional transmission scenario, DOE reports modeled present-value savings through 2050 of about $320 billion in power-system costs, $730 billion in climate damages, and $50 billion in health damages, with about 3,420 million metric tons of avoided greenhouse-gas emissions.
sources.limitations: Scenario results are not observed benefits or guaranteed outcomes; health benefits depend on the displaced generation and population exposure.

sources.title: Power Lines and Wildlife
sources.claim_verification: Summarizes direct and indirect wildlife effects including collision, habitat avoidance and fragmentation, and altered predator access, while noting important uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Overview rather than a project-specific impact assessment.
